memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Do for Aaron and his sons everything I have commanded you, taking seven days to ordain them. Sacrifice a bull each day as a sin offering to make atonement. Purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it." - Exodus 29:35-36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The ordination took seven days. Not an afternoon, not a single ceremony, but a full week of repeated sacrifice and consecration. God could have accomplished it in a moment. Instead He stretched it across seven days of daily offerings.

God is often unhurried with us. We prefer instant transformation — one prayer, one conference, one decisive moment, and the work is finished. But God frequently works through repetition and time, day after day, until something is genuinely formed rather than merely begun. The seven days were not inefficiency; they were formation.

Paul was confident that He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus (Phil 1:6). Note the words "carry it on" — a continuing process, not a single event. If you are frustrated that you are not further along, remember Aaron's seven days. God is not in a hurry, and slow work is not failed work. Show up again tomorrow. The daily repetition is how consecration actually happens.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I frustrated that God is working more slowly in me than I would like?
What daily, repeated practice is God asking me to keep showing up for?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You work through days and repetition, not only through moments. Give me patience with Your pace and faithfulness to keep showing up while You do Your work in me. Amen.
